brief: A hotter than expected September core CPI (+33bps vs 20bps consensus, driven by firmer shelter) pushed the market to rebuild near-term Fed hike risk from compressed front-end pricing, with odds now 35% for October and 87% for December. GIR continues to expect a second hike in December, with tomorrow's PPI and Warsh's Bangkok speech as near-term tells. That CPI surprise catalyzed the session's broad index drawdown (SPX -111bps to 7,719, first -1% SPX/-2% NDX move since late July), spearheaded by AI-trade de-risking: neocloud stocks fell 12% (a top-5 move in 5 years) and hyperscaler bond yields drew focus amid credit-market doubts about financing the AI trade, layered onto OpenAI revenue confusion, China memory easing bottlenecks, datacenter sentiment into the midterms, power/shell constraints and further issuance. Asset managers and hedge funds were net sellers on overlapping tech and macro supply, with the info-tech sell skew at a 4-week high and ETF volumes +40-60%, read as top-down selling, though desk activity was only 4/10. In options, price action lacked capitulation. The skew curve steepened, and the desk reads this as cutting the AI trade's right tail rather than panic, with flows tilted to hedging and vol still seen as too cheap.
